title.value: Subject-Based Domain Adaptation for Facial Expression Recognition
title.justification: The paper addresses a specific approach for domain adaptation in facial expression recognition, focusing on adapting models to specific individuals using subject-based domain adaptation techniques.
title.quote: This paper introduces a new MSDA method for subject-based domain adaptation in FER. It efficiently leverages information from multiple source subjects (labeled source domain data) to adapt a deep FER model to a single target individual (unlabeled target domain data).

analysis.description: The paper introduces a novel multi-source domain adaptation method for facial expression recognition, enabling adaptation of deep learning models to specific individuals by treating each subject as a separate domain. It utilizes a strategy for generating pseudo-labels to improve domain shift adaptation, tested on datasets like BioVid and UNBC-McMaster.

type.justification: The paper conducts experiments on challenging datasets like BioVid and UNBC-McMaster to validate the proposed methods for subject-based domain adaptation.
type.quote: Experiments performed on the challenging BioVid heat and pain dataset with 87 subjects and the UNBC-McMaster shoulder pain dataset with 25 subjects show that our subject-based MSDA can outperform state-of-the-art methods yet scale well to multiple subject-based source domains.

name.justification: The research primarily deals with facial expression recognition, a sub-field of computer vision, and proposes methods for improving model adaptation to individual subject variances.
name.quote: Adapting a deep learning model to a specific target individual is a challenging facial expression recognition (FER) task.

name.justification: Facial Expression Recognition (FER) is the main application domain where the proposed subject-based domain adaptation method is applied.
name.quote: Adapting a deep learning model to a specific target individual is a challenging facial expression recognition (FER) task.

name.justification: The paper focuses on domain adaptation techniques, specifically multi-source domain adaptation for facial expression recognition.
name.quote: Unlike UDA, multi-source domain adaptation (MSDA) methods can leverage multiple source datasets to improve the accuracy and robustness of the target model.

name.justification: The experiments conducted in the paper utilize ResNet18 as the backbone model for training and adaptation processes.
name.quote: In all experiments, we use the ResNet18 [11] backbone pre-trained on ImageNet by removing the first ReLU and MaxPool layers and the last 2D adaptive average pooling layer.

is_contributed.justification: ResNet18 is a standard model used for evaluation and not a contribution of the paper.
